justification: Wires the may-apply block: 52 reviewed areas loaded, the route returns them in meta.may_apply beside the provisions, the page renders them. Adds a block and removes chapters from the council-wide notice only where the block shows the rules; no property provision, count or TOC changes. Not Critical: no DB write, no regulatory value hand-typed (every suburb and quote is from the draft file).

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The shared JSON the route reads is not the exact export of the data file (an area or suburb edited in one place only).
falsifiable_check.external_authority: data/chapter_scope/suburb_unconfirmed_areas.json, built from the reviewed draft t2-2-areas-2026-10-20.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed red: changing one area's suburbs in the data file to a test value made test_shared_file_matches_data_file fail; restored, 4 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: DcpMayApplyBlock, may-apply-reasons and export_may_apply_areas.py already existed; this wires them. getNotCovered / DcpNotCoveredNotice are the council-wide list that is now filtered.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: parseStreet returns the street name as string[], but suburbFromAddress called .trim() on it (tsc TS2339, throws for an address without a comma); fixed to use the token count.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One new lib (may-apply-query.ts) so the 1,600-line route gains only a call; reuses PROVISION_BASE_SELECT, withCouncilWords and withServedCitation so rows look like served rows.
pre_impl.frontend_type: MayApplyArea gains optional chapter_key so the notice can drop a chapter shown in the block.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A reader in a listed suburb sees an amber collapsed block with the withheld rules and why we cannot place the lot, instead of nothing.

functions.name: loadMayApply
functions.output: A list of areas, each with its rule rows or null when that lookup failed
functions.if_none: [] when no council, no suburb or no listed area
functions.failure_mode: a failed select gives that area provisions: null, never []

queries.purpose: rows of one area, withheld rows included
queries.where_clause: is_current = TRUE AND source_council=$1 AND source_chapter_key=$2 AND (pdf_page BETWEEN $3 AND $4 OR id = ANY($5)) AND v2_provision_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'TOC' AND v2_dcp_layer IS NOT NULL; no v2_is_actionable test on purpose; LIMIT 400

break_it.what_happens: That area returns provisions: null; the block says it could not load; the rest of the page is served

break_it.scenario: Manly lot in a Northern Beaches suburb
break_it.how: northern_beaches requires land application status covered or partial

break_it.scenario: The suburb is sent with a postcode or in lower case
break_it.what_happens: It is normalised to the same key as the data file, so the area is still found
break_it.how: normaliseSuburb on both sides, matched by the drift test
break_it.repro: may-apply-meta.test.ts first case sends 'suburb nsw 2000' in lower case

verified: tsc --noEmit: no errors in changed files (one pre-existing @react-pdf/renderer missing-module error in ProvisionsByTocStructure.tsx, environment only).
gaps: Jest not run locally (jest is not installed in the worktree); 3 jest files unexecuted.
The SQL was not run against the database.

post_merge.manual_verify: Open an address in a listed suburb and confirm the block, then one outside it and confirm none.
